heading: Where do I start?
lead: Pick the role you want to grow into. Each roadmap is six stages in order: what to learn, the first decision you'll face there, and a project that proves you're ready to move on.
principle: A roadmap is a starting order, not a checklist to finish. Build something at every stage — you'll learn more from one shipped project than from ten tutorials.

home.title: Start with a roadmap
home.body: Six career paths for beginners, each in six stages, linked to the decisions you'll meet on the way.

web-developer.label: Web Developer
web-developer.summary: Build and ship complete websites, from the page in the browser to the server behind it.
web-developer.outcome: A full-stack app of your own, live on a real domain, that you can explain end to end.
web-developer.pace: 9–12 months at about 10 hours a week

how-the-web-works.title: How the web works
how-the-web-works.goal: Understand what happens between typing a URL and seeing a page, so later tools don't feel like magic.

skills.name: DNS, TCP and HTTP
skills.note: How a request finds a server and gets an answer

skills.name: Status codes and headers
skills.note: What 200, 301, 404 and 500 tell you

skills.name: Browser DevTools
skills.note: The Network tab shows every request a page makes

skills.name: Command line and Git
skills.note: Move around files and save your work's history

how-the-web-works.decision: Do I need a framework yet?
how-the-web-works.advice: No. Frameworks hide the parts you're learning here. Pick one only once you can say what it saves you from.
how-the-web-works.project: Open the Network tab on a site you use daily and explain every request it makes on load.

html-css.title: HTML and CSS
html-css.goal: Structure content with meaning and lay it out so it works on every screen.

skills.name: Semantic HTML
skills.note: Headings, lists and forms that mean something

skills.name: Flexbox and Grid
skills.note: Lay out rows, columns and whole pages

skills.name: Responsive design
skills.note: One layout that works from phone to desktop

skills.name: Accessibility basics
skills.note: Labels, contrast and keyboard use

html-css.advice: Plain CSS first, until you can read what a utility class does. Then use whichever your team uses.
html-css.project: Rebuild a real landing page from a screenshot, responsive down to phone width.

javascript.title: JavaScript
javascript.goal: Make pages interactive and talk to other services.

skills.name: Language basics
skills.note: Variables, functions, arrays and objects

skills.name: DOM and events
skills.note: Change the page when the user does something

skills.name: Async code
skills.note: fetch, Promises and async/await

skills.name: Modules and npm
skills.note: Split code into files and use packages

javascript.advice: JavaScript first. Move to TypeScript once a type bug has cost you an afternoon — you'll know exactly what it's for.
javascript.project: A search page that calls a public API and handles loading, empty and error states.

frontend-framework.title: A frontend framework
frontend-framework.goal: Build larger interfaces out of components, with state and routing.

skills.name: Components and props
skills.note: Reusable pieces of interface

skills.name: State and effects
skills.note: Data that changes, and what reacts to it

skills.name: Routing
skills.note: Several pages in one app, with real URLs

skills.name: Forms and validation
skills.note: Collect input and explain what's wrong

frontend-framework.advice: Pick the one with the most job posts where you want to work. Components, state and routing transfer between all three.
frontend-framework.project: A multi-page app with routing, a form, and data from an API.

backend-and-data.title: Backend and database
backend-and-data.goal: Store data, expose it through an API and know who is asking.

skills.name: A server language
skills.note: Node.js is the shortest step from JavaScript

skills.name: REST APIs and JSON
skills.note: Endpoints other programs can call

skills.name: SQL and relations
skills.note: Tables, joins and keeping data consistent

skills.name: Authentication and CORS
skills.note: Know who's calling and from where

backend-and-data.advice: For a single web app, session cookies are simpler and safer. Reach for JWT when several services must verify the same user.
backend-and-data.project: An API with sign-up, login and create/read/update/delete, backed by PostgreSQL.

ship-it.title: Deploy and maintain
ship-it.goal: Put your app on the internet and keep it running.

skills.name: Hosting and HTTPS
skills.note: Domains, certificates and where the app runs

skills.name: Environment variables
skills.note: Keep secrets and settings out of the code

skills.name: Logs and health checks
skills.note: Know when something breaks, and why

skills.name: Continuous integration
skills.note: Tests run automatically on every push

ship-it.decision: A platform (PaaS) or my own server?
ship-it.advice: A platform first. Running your own server teaches a lot, but it's a second project — ship the first one.
ship-it.project: Deploy your full-stack app to a custom domain, with CI that runs on every push.

frontend-developer.label: Frontend Developer
frontend-developer.summary: Build fast, accessible interfaces that people enjoy using.
frontend-developer.outcome: A portfolio of interfaces that are fast, accessible and tested, built with a modern framework.
frontend-developer.pace: 6–9 months at about 10 hours a week

foundations.title: HTML, CSS and accessibility
foundations.goal: Master the platform every framework compiles down to.

skills.name: Semantic HTML
skills.note: Structure that browsers and screen readers understand

skills.name: Flexbox and Grid
skills.note: Responsive layouts without hacks

skills.name: CSS custom properties
skills.note: Themes, dark mode and design tokens

skills.name: Keyboard and screen readers
skills.note: Test that everyone can use the page

foundations.advice: Learn plain CSS well, then adopt the team's choice. CSS Modules, Tailwind and CSS-in-JS are all fine once the basics are solid.
foundations.project: Three responsive pages that pass a keyboard-only and screen-reader walkthrough.

javascript-deep.title: JavaScript in depth
javascript-deep.goal: Understand the language well enough to debug what a framework does.

skills.name: Scope and closures
skills.note: Why a function remembers its variables

skills.name: The event loop
skills.note: How Promises and async/await really run

skills.name: Modules and bundlers
skills.note: How Vite turns files into a fast app

skills.name: TypeScript basics
skills.note: Catch mistakes before the browser does

javascript-deep.advice: As soon as a project has more than a few files. The editor help alone pays for itself.
javascript-deep.project: A small vanilla TypeScript app, such as a to-do list with filters and local storage.

framework.title: A framework: React
framework.goal: Build interfaces from components and manage state predictably.

skills.name: Components and JSX
skills.note: Describe the interface as a function of data

skills.name: Hooks
skills.note: State, effects and refs inside components

skills.name: Routing
skills.note: Pages, links and state kept in the URL

skills.name: Forms
skills.note: Controlled inputs and validation

framework.advice: In the component that uses it. Lift it up when two siblings need it; add a global store only when distant parts of the app do.
framework.project: A dashboard with routes, filters kept in the URL, and a form that validates.

data-fetching.title: Talking to APIs
data-fetching.goal: Load, cache and update server data without breaking the interface.

skills.name: Loading and error states
skills.note: Never leave the user looking at a blank screen

skills.name: Caching and refetching
skills.note: TanStack Query or similar data libraries

skills.name: Pagination
skills.note: Pages, cursors and infinite scroll

skills.name: CORS and auth headers
skills.note: Why the browser blocks some requests

data-fetching.decision: Fetch in effects, or use a data library?
data-fetching.advice: Write it by hand once to feel the pain, then use a data library. It solves caching, retries and races you'd otherwise rebuild.
data-fetching.project: A paginated list with search that caches results and recovers from a failed request.

rendering-performance.title: Rendering and performance
rendering-performance.goal: Make pages load fast and stay smooth on slow phones.

skills.name: CSR vs SSR
skills.note: Where the HTML is built, and why it matters

skills.name: Core Web Vitals
skills.note: Measure load, interactivity and layout shift

skills.name: Code splitting
skills.note: Ship only the code the page needs

skills.name: Images and fonts
skills.note: Usually the heaviest part of a page

rendering-performance.advice: Only if the first load or search ranking matters for this page. A dashboard behind a login usually doesn't need it.
rendering-performance.project: Take an existing app, measure it, and cut its largest contentful paint in half.

testing-shipping.title: Testing and shipping
testing-shipping.goal: Change code with confidence and release it safely.

skills.name: Unit tests
skills.note: Vitest or Jest for logic and helpers

skills.name: Component tests
skills.note: Testing Library, the way users see it

skills.name: End-to-end tests
skills.note: Playwright drives a real browser

skills.name: CI and feature flags
skills.note: Merge often, release when ready

testing-shipping.advice: The flows that make money or lose data: sign-in, checkout, saving. One end-to-end test there beats a hundred snapshot tests.
testing-shipping.project: Add CI with tests to your dashboard and ship one feature behind a flag.

backend-developer.label: Backend Developer
backend-developer.summary: Design the APIs, data and services that applications run on.
backend-developer.outcome: A production-ready API with a database, authentication, caching and monitoring.
backend-developer.pace: 9–12 months at about 10 hours a week

language.title: One language, deeply
language.goal: Get fluent in one server language and the tools around it.

skills.name: One language
skills.note: Node.js, Python, Go or Java

skills.name: Packages and testing
skills.note: The tools every project in it uses

skills.name: Git and the command line
skills.note: Daily tools on every team

skills.name: Linux basics
skills.note: Files, processes and permissions on servers

language.advice: The one most used by companies you'd like to work for. The concepts carry over; switching later takes weeks, not years.
language.project: A command-line tool that reads a file, transforms it and has tests.

http-apis.title: HTTP and APIs
http-apis.goal: Design APIs that are predictable for the people who call them.

skills.name: REST design
skills.note: Resources, status codes and consistent errors

skills.name: Input validation
skills.note: Never trust what the client sends

skills.name: Idempotency
skills.note: Make retries safe for callers

skills.name: Rate limiting and docs
skills.note: Protect the API and describe it with OpenAPI

http-apis.advice: REST, unless many different clients need very different shapes of the same data. It is simpler to cache, secure and debug.
http-apis.project: A documented REST API for a small domain (a library, a shop) with validation and consistent errors.

databases.title: Databases
databases.goal: Model data correctly and query it without surprises.

skills.name: SQL
skills.note: Joins, aggregates and transactions

skills.name: Schema and migrations
skills.note: Change the database safely over time

skills.name: Indexes and query plans
skills.note: Find out why a query is slow

skills.name: ORMs
skills.note: Use them without hiding the SQL they run

databases.advice: PostgreSQL by default. Choose something else when you can name the access pattern it serves better.
databases.project: Back your API with PostgreSQL, with migrations and an index you justified with EXPLAIN.

auth-security.title: Authentication and security
auth-security.goal: Know who is calling and keep their data safe.

skills.name: Password hashing
skills.note: bcrypt or Argon2, never plain text

skills.name: Sessions, JWT and OAuth
skills.note: Ways to remember who signed in

skills.name: OWASP Top 10
skills.note: The most common ways apps get attacked

skills.name: Secrets management
skills.note: Keys and passwords out of the repository

auth-security.decision: Build auth myself, or use a provider?
auth-security.advice: Build it once to learn it, then use a proven library or provider in production. Auth bugs are expensive and quiet.
auth-security.project: Add sign-up, login, roles and password reset to your API.

caching-async.title: Caching and background work
caching-async.goal: Keep responses fast and move slow work out of the request.

skills.name: Caching with Redis
skills.note: Serve repeated reads without the database

skills.name: Job queues
skills.note: Workers handle slow tasks like email

skills.name: Retries with backoff
skills.note: Recover from failures without piling on

skills.name: Message brokers
skills.note: When Kafka or RabbitMQ is worth it

caching-async.decision: Do I need Redis or Kafka yet?
caching-async.advice: Probably not. Measure first; add a cache when a query is proven slow, and a broker when a database-backed queue can't keep up.
caching-async.project: Send emails from a background worker and cache one slow endpoint — with numbers before and after.

production.title: Running in production
production.goal: Deploy, observe and scale a service you're responsible for.

skills.name: Docker and deployment
skills.note: Run the same build everywhere

skills.name: Logs, metrics and alerts
skills.note: See what the service is doing

skills.name: Pools and graceful shutdown
skills.note: Don't drop requests during a deploy

skills.name: Scaling out
skills.note: More instances when one isn't enough

production.advice: A monolith. Split a service out when a team or a scaling need forces it, not before.
production.project: Deploy your API with a health check, a dashboard and one alert that would wake you up for the right reason.

mobile-developer.label: Mobile Developer
mobile-developer.summary: Build apps for Android and iOS that feel at home on a phone.
mobile-developer.outcome: An app published on a store, with offline support and push notifications.
mobile-developer.pace: 8–12 months at about 10 hours a week

programming-basics.title: Programming fundamentals
programming-basics.goal: Learn to write code before learning to write apps.

skills.name: One language
skills.note: Dart, Kotlin, Swift or JavaScript

skills.name: Types and classes
skills.note: Model the data your app works with

skills.name: Asynchronous code
skills.note: Wait for the network without freezing

skills.name: Git basics
skills.note: Save and share your work

programming-basics.advice: Choose after the next stage's decision if you can: Dart for Flutter, Kotlin for Android, Swift for iOS, JavaScript for React Native.
programming-basics.project: A small console program, such as a quiz or budget tracker, with tests.

choose-approach.title: Native or cross-platform
choose-approach.goal: Pick the approach that fits the apps you want to build.

skills.name: Native
skills.note: Kotlin with Jetpack Compose, Swift with SwiftUI

skills.name: Cross-platform
skills.note: Flutter or React Native, one codebase

skills.name: Emulators and devices
skills.note: Run your app where users will

skills.name: Building and signing
skills.note: How an app becomes an installable file

choose-approach.advice: Cross-platform if you want both stores with one codebase. Native if you target one platform or need deep device features.
choose-approach.project: Run a hello-world app on a real phone, not only the emulator.

screens.title: Building screens
screens.goal: Lay out screens that follow each platform's conventions.

skills.name: Layouts and lists
skills.note: Scrolling content that stays smooth

skills.name: Navigation
skills.note: Moving between screens and back

skills.name: Platform guidelines
skills.note: Material Design and Apple's HIG

skills.name: Screen sizes
skills.note: Small phones, large phones and tablets

screens.decision: One design for both platforms, or native looks?
screens.advice: Shared brand, native behaviour: keep your colours and type, but let back navigation and gestures feel like the platform.
screens.project: A three-screen app (list, detail, settings) with navigation.

state-data.title: State and data
state-data.goal: Load data from the network and keep the app usable offline.

skills.name: State management
skills.note: Keep screens in sync with the data

skills.name: HTTP and JSON
skills.note: Talk to your backend API

skills.name: Local storage
skills.note: SQLite and key-value stores on the device

skills.name: Offline sync
skills.note: Queue changes and retry when back online

state-data.advice: At least reading what the user has already seen. Decide early — offline support is hard to add later.
state-data.project: Connect your app to an API, cache the data locally and handle a lost connection.

device-features.title: Device features
device-features.goal: Use what makes phones special, with the user's permission.

skills.name: Permissions
skills.note: Ask at the right moment, handle a “no”

skills.name: Camera and uploads
skills.note: Photos and files over slow networks

skills.name: Location and maps
skills.note: Where the user is, used carefully

skills.name: Push notifications
skills.note: Bring users back without annoying them

device-features.decision: When should I ask for permission?
device-features.advice: At the moment the feature is used, with a reason on screen. Asking on first launch gets a “no”.
device-features.project: Add a photo upload with progress and a push notification to your app.

publish.title: Testing and publishing
publish.goal: Ship to real users and keep the app stable.

skills.name: Unit and UI tests
skills.note: Catch regressions before users do

skills.name: Crash reporting
skills.note: Know about crashes the moment they happen

skills.name: Store submission
skills.note: Play Store and App Store reviews

skills.name: Staged rollouts
skills.note: Release to a few users first, with flags

publish.decision: When is it ready to publish?
publish.advice: When the core flow works and crashes are reported to you. Publish small and early; real users find what testers don't.
publish.project: Publish your app to at least one store with crash reporting turned on.

ux-ui-designer.label: UX/UI Designer
ux-ui-designer.summary: Understand people's problems and design interfaces that solve them.
ux-ui-designer.outcome: A portfolio of case studies that show your process, from research to a tested design.
ux-ui-designer.pace: 6–9 months at about 10 hours a week

ux-foundations.title: UX foundations
ux-foundations.goal: Start from the user's problem, not from the screen.

skills.name: User research
skills.note: Interviews that uncover real needs

skills.name: Personas and jobs to be done
skills.note: Who you design for, and what they need done

skills.name: Problem statements
skills.note: Name the problem before any solution

skills.name: Design thinking
skills.note: Understand, explore, test, repeat

ux-foundations.advice: Talk to five users first. It takes a few days and stops you polishing a solution to the wrong problem.
ux-foundations.project: Interview five people about a daily task and write the problem you'd solve.

flows-wireframes.title: Flows and wireframes
flows-wireframes.goal: Organise content and steps before deciding how anything looks.

skills.name: Information architecture
skills.note: Group and name content so people find it

skills.name: User flows
skills.note: The steps from a goal to done

skills.name: Wireframes
skills.note: Low-fidelity layouts, quick to change

skills.name: Card sorting
skills.note: Let users show how they group things

flows-wireframes.advice: Paper for the first ideas — they're cheap to throw away. Move to digital once the flow is settled.
flows-wireframes.project: Wireframe the full flow for the problem from stage one.

visual-design.title: Visual design
visual-design.goal: Make interfaces clear, consistent and pleasant to use.

skills.name: Typography
skills.note: Type sizes and weights that create hierarchy

skills.name: Colour and contrast
skills.note: Meaningful, readable and on-brand

skills.name: Spacing and grids
skills.note: Consistent rhythm and alignment

skills.name: Icons and imagery
skills.note: Support the content, don't decorate it

visual-design.advice: Fewer than you think: one or two typefaces, one accent colour, and a strict spacing scale.
visual-design.project: Turn your wireframes into high-fidelity screens with a simple style guide.

prototyping.title: Figma and prototyping
prototyping.goal: Build designs that behave like the real product.

skills.name: Auto Layout
skills.note: Frames that resize like real interfaces

skills.name: Components and variants
skills.note: Design once, reuse everywhere

skills.name: Interactive prototypes
skills.note: Clickable flows to test with users

skills.name: Mobile and desktop
skills.note: Adapt one design to both sizes

prototyping.decision: How realistic should a prototype be?
prototyping.advice: Only as realistic as the question you're testing needs. Test the flow in grey boxes before the colours.
prototyping.project: A clickable prototype of your core flow, on mobile and desktop.

accessibility-systems.title: Accessibility and design systems
accessibility-systems.goal: Design for everyone and at scale.

skills.name: WCAG basics
skills.note: Contrast ratios and readable text sizes

skills.name: Focus and keyboard paths
skills.note: Usable without a mouse

skills.name: Design tokens
skills.note: Colours and spacing as named values

skills.name: Component libraries
skills.note: Shared parts for designers and developers

accessibility-systems.decision: Use an existing design system, or build one?
accessibility-systems.advice: Start from an existing one (Material, a Figma UI kit) and adapt it. Build your own when a product outgrows it.
accessibility-systems.project: Turn your screens into a small design system with tokens and accessible components.

testing-handoff.title: Usability testing and handoff
testing-handoff.goal: Prove the design works and help developers build it.

skills.name: Usability testing
skills.note: Watch real people try your design

skills.name: Success metrics
skills.note: Task completion and time on task

skills.name: Developer handoff
skills.note: Specs, states and edge cases

skills.name: Case studies
skills.note: Show your process in your portfolio

testing-handoff.decision: How do I know the design is good?
testing-handoff.advice: Watch five users try the core task without help. Where they hesitate is where the design needs work, not where they say it does.
testing-handoff.project: Test your prototype with five users, fix what they struggled with, and publish it as a case study.

devops.label: DevOps Engineer
devops.summary: Automate how software is built, deployed and kept running.
devops.outcome: An automated pipeline that tests, deploys and monitors an app on cloud infrastructure you defined in code.
devops.pace: 9–12 months at about 10 hours a week

linux-networking.title: Linux and networking
linux-networking.goal: Be at home on a server and understand how machines talk.

skills.name: The shell
skills.note: Files, processes and permissions

skills.name: SSH and packages
skills.note: Reach servers and install software safely

skills.name: IP, ports and DNS
skills.note: How machines find and reach each other

skills.name: HTTP, TLS and Nginx
skills.note: Serve sites securely behind a reverse proxy

linux-networking.advice: Ubuntu or Debian. What matters is the skills, and they transfer to every distribution.
linux-networking.project: Set up a Linux server, secure SSH, and serve a site over HTTPS with Nginx.

scripting-git.title: Scripting and version control
scripting-git.goal: Automate the task you'd otherwise do by hand twice.

skills.name: Bash scripting
skills.note: Glue commands into repeatable scripts

skills.name: Python for automation
skills.note: When a script needs real logic

skills.name: Git workflows
skills.note: Branches, pull requests and reviews

skills.name: YAML and JSON
skills.note: The formats every tool is configured in

scripting-git.advice: Bash for gluing commands together, Python once a script needs logic, error handling or tests.
scripting-git.project: A script that backs up a directory, rotates old backups and reports failures.

containers.title: Containers
containers.goal: Package apps so they run the same everywhere.

skills.name: Dockerfiles
skills.note: Build an image for your app

skills.name: Docker Compose
skills.note: Run an app with its database and network

skills.name: Small, secure images
skills.note: Fewer layers, fewer vulnerabilities

skills.name: Health checks
skills.note: Let the platform know the app is alive

containers.advice: Not until one server with Docker Compose isn't enough. Kubernetes solves problems a beginner doesn't have yet.
containers.project: Containerise an app with its database using Docker Compose.

ci-cd.title: CI/CD
ci-cd.goal: Make every change tested and deployable automatically.

skills.name: Pipelines
skills.note: GitHub Actions or GitLab CI

skills.name: Tests and image builds
skills.note: Every merge produces a tested artifact

skills.name: Deployment strategies
skills.note: Rolling, blue-green and canary releases

skills.name: Rollbacks and flags
skills.note: Undo a bad release in minutes

ci-cd.advice: Yes, once tests and a quick rollback exist. Small, frequent deploys are safer than big rare ones.
ci-cd.project: A pipeline that tests, builds and deploys your containerised app on every merge.

cloud-iac.title: Cloud and infrastructure as code
cloud-iac.goal: Create cloud infrastructure you can review, repeat and destroy.

skills.name: One cloud
skills.note: AWS, Google Cloud or Azure

skills.name: Networking and IAM
skills.note: Least privilege from day one

skills.name: Terraform
skills.note: Infrastructure you can review in a pull request

skills.name: Managed services and cost
skills.note: Know what you run and what it costs

cloud-iac.advice: Scale up first — a bigger machine is one change. Scale out when you need redundancy or have hit the biggest machine.
cloud-iac.project: Define your app's infrastructure in Terraform and recreate it from scratch.

observability.title: Observability and reliability
observability.goal: Know something is wrong before users tell you, and recover fast.

skills.name: Logs, metrics and traces
skills.note: Three views of what a system is doing

skills.name: Prometheus and Grafana
skills.note: Collect metrics and build dashboards

skills.name: Alerting
skills.note: Page people only for what users feel

skills.name: Backups and incidents
skills.note: Restore data and learn from outages

observability.advice: Symptoms users feel — errors, latency, a full disk — not every CPU spike. An alert nobody acts on trains people to ignore alerts.
observability.project: A dashboard and alerts for your app, and a tested restore from backup.
